findings.title: Shared UniPoolerCutoverCore step 2 has no recovery branch: a 2-wei donate+sync on the permissionless canonical sUSDS/phUSD pair makes the mainnet cutover core revert for good
findings.description: Core step 2 requires the canonical pair's reserves to be (0,0) both before and after an optional skim, and there is no other branch. Uniswap V2 reserves set by sync() can never return to (0,0) once LP totalSupply is 0: skim() does not touch reserves and burn() needs LP. yield-claim-nft:051's constructor check (UniPoolerV2__PairNotCanonical) binds UniPoolerV2 to factory.getPair(sUSDS, phUSD), so the pooler cannot be pointed at a different pair. Any third party can therefore createPair today (mainnet getPair == 0 at block 26109485), transfer 1 wei of each token and call sync(). After that, every run of the shared core reverts at step 2. The core is inherited by the dev rehearsal (story 101) and by the future mainnet cutover script and fork test (story 103), so this defect propagates to the mainnet operation. docs/BalancerWinddownPlan.md §4 (lines 410-414) discusses only in-window griefing between steps 1 and 6, and points to a recovery helper (transfer + pair.mint(UniPoolerV2) with a price check) that does not exist in the core. Pre-emptive poisoning before the run starts is not addressed.
findings.impact: Availability of the Balancexit index-4 cutover, not funds. The revert happens in forge's simulation, before any broadcast, so nothing is half-done. But the 103 script as built on this core cannot run at all until someone writes, reviews and broadcasts a bespoke seeding path under the Balancer wind-down timeline. The griefer's cost is 2 wei plus gas. A recovery exists outside the core (send the recovered tokens to the pair, then pair.mint(newPooler): with LP totalSupply 0 the first minter takes all LP and the griefer's dust is absorbed), which caps severity at Low.
findings.evidence: side-effects.json mainnetForkProbe.tests[1] (test_B_dustSyncedPairPermanentlyBlocksCoreStep2 PASS at block 26109485: reserves (1,1) after sync, pair totalSupply 0, unchanged after skim, core reverts 'UniPoolerCutoverCore: pair reserves not empty'); live read getPair(sUSDS, phUSD) == 0x0. Test A (same file) shows the core otherwise completes on live state.
findings.propagation: Law-1 relevant beyond dev: same code is the planned mainnet cutover (story 103, incomplete).
findings.recommendation: Add a pre-poisoned-pair branch to the core instead of relaxing the router path. When reserves != 0 AND pair.totalSupply() == 0, do NOT seed through Router02, because it would quote against griefer-set reserves. Instead, from ONE transaction via a small reviewed helper contract (never two owner txs, since anyone can call pair.mint(to) after a bare transfer and take all the LP), transfer all recovered sUSDS/phUSD to the pair, call pair.mint(newPooler), and then require: (a) the post-mint reserve ratio is within seedToleranceBps of the Balancer exit ratio (sAmt:pAmt), (b) the pre-existing reserves are below an explicit dust bound, and (c) newPooler holds totalSupply - MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY. Keep the strict (0,0) path when totalSupply == 0 and reserves == 0. Revert, as today, when totalSupply > 0 or the reserves exceed the dust bound. Better still, do createPair-if-missing, the skim check and the transfer+mint seed atomically in the helper, which also closes the step-2-to-6 window. Add a core unit test that pre-syncs (1,1) and expects the branch to succeed with the ratio check enforced, plus a test where a large skewed pre-sync fails the ratio check. Land it in the shared core before the story-103 broadcast.

classification.assetImpact: No assets are at risk. The revert happens in forge's local simulation of core step 2, before any broadcast, so nothing is half-executed and the recovered sUSDS/phUSD never leave the Balancer position. classifiedFinding.justification: Rated Low, not Medium. It is flagged for human review because the sanitizer argued for Medium. The case for Medium is a cheap, permissionless and permanent DoS of a mainnet-bound migration core, which is a fair Law-1 availability argument, and nothing here dismisses it. It still falls short of C4 Medium for four reasons. (1) No asset is at risk, and protocol function is not impaired: index-4 mints keep working on BalancerPoolerV2, and the Balancer exit stays open through recovery mode after both BIP-928 deadlines, so the delay costs at most idle sUSDS (opportunity cost), not principal. (2) The revert is fail-loud in simulation before any broadcast, so nothing is half-wired. (3) 'Permanent' applies only to the strict require in this script core, not to the pair. An atomic transfer+mint seed absorbs the dust, and once LP totalSupply > 0 further dust-syncs cannot block a mint-based seed, so the grief cannot be repeated against the fix. (4) The workaround is a script-level change, and the wind-down plan already describes it (for the post-step-2 case). The gap was also already raised in story 108's own review as a [Low-Medium, doc] finding and accepted non-blocking by the human. This is disclosed for transparency; that review is not a ledger disposition, so it does not suppress this finding, and the finding stays open because the core still has no branch for it. Re-weigh to Medium if index-4 or the Balancer exit stops working while the cutover is blocked, or if the deadline pressure becomes a value loss rather than a delay. The check itself is load-bearing: Router02.addLiquidity quotes against existing reserves, so any relaxation that seeds through the router would let the griefer choose the opening price. The recommendation keeps that protection.

Keep the strict (0,0) path when totalSupply == 0 and reserves == 0. Revert, as today, when totalSupply > 0 or the reserves exceed the dust bound. Better still, do createPair-if-missing, the skim check and the transfer+mint seed atomically in the helper, which also closes the step-2-to-6 window. Add a core unit test that pre-syncs (1,1) and expects the branch to succeed with the ratio check enforced, plus a test where a large skewed pre-sync fails the ratio check. Land it in the shared core before the story-103 broadcast.

findings.title: Phase 9.7's 'minter principal cleared from the legacy strategy' post-condition holds only in forge's simulation; on the broadcast chain 1.2e13 wei of minter principal stays on the de-registered legacy DOLA strategy
findings.severityNote: Dust-sized on a mock chain; may classify as QA. Filed because the script's own require certifies a state the chain does not have.
findings.description: Story 089 requires the minter's DOLA collateral to move off the legacy (MockAutoDOLA) strategy. Phase 9.7 reads principalOf(minter) and passes that number to withdrawAsOwner, then require()s principalOf == 0. forge evaluates both during the simulation pass, where the whole run shares one timestamp, and bakes the amount (5000e18) into calldata. On the broadcast chain (anvil --block-time 2), MockAutoDOLA's time-based _updateYield runs between blocks, so ERC4626YieldStrategy._acquireShares (convertToAssets) credits 5000.000011999712006910e18 at the block-434 minter.mint. The block-436 withdrawAsOwner(5000e18) leaves 11,999,712,006,910 wei behind. The require never runs on chain.
findings.impact: The local end state differs from what dev asserts and logs ('Phase 9.7 end state asserted'). The minter stays the sole principal holder on a strategy that SYA no longer lists and cannot withdraw from, so legacy totalBalanceOf(minter) = 3,299.64 DOLA (all mock yield, including simulate-yield's 2,300) accrues to an unreachable bucket. More broadly, it is a concrete instance where a simulation-time self-assert passes over time-dependent state while the chain diverges.
findings.evidence: side-effects.json stateWrites (YieldStrategyDolaLegacy principal: block 435 = 5000.000011999712006910e18, block 436+ = 11999712006910) and postconditionResults; broadcast txs 433-436 (approve, PhusdStableMinter.mint 5000e18, MockDola.mint, withdrawAsOwner(minter, deployer, 5000e18)); dev-run.filtered.log line for Phase 9.7 shows principal 5000e18 in simulation.
findings.recommendation: Withdraw against the on-chain principal rather than a simulation-time number. Pass type(uint256).max (withdrawAsOwner caps to the available principal in AYieldStrategy._withdrawInternal), or principal plus a margin, and re-seed the deployer's actual DOLA delta. Alternatively, accept and log residual dust explicitly instead of asserting principalOf == 0.
